events.text: The council gathers. Mission 1 begins.

Zara proposes Elena, Felix. A two-person mission gives maximum information: the revealed number of Fail cards equals the number of evil players on the team. By putting Elena (whose alignment I can confirm to myself) alongside one unconfirmed player, the fail count tells me definitively whether that second player is evil or good. Felix is a reasonable, low-risk pick to pair with, and this also puts a known evil on the board where she can help push for failure if needed.

I oppose the proposed team of Elena and Felix. Zara’s own rationale says this places “a known evil” on the team who can “help push for failure if needed”; that is not a basis I can approve for Mission 1. Even setting that wording aside, Elena is the unconfirmed pick whose card would be most informative only if paired with someone I trust, and Felix does not give me that certainty. I would rather see a revised team that excludes Elena and gives a clearer reason to trust Felix. I will vote against this proposal.

I know I’m good, but I can’t verify Elena’s alignment. Zara’s rationale explicitly describes placing a known evil player on the team, which gives me serious reason to oppose this proposal. Zara, can you explain why you described the team that way?

Felix, you asked me to explain my wording, so let me be plain: I phrased that badly, and I owe the council a better rationale. What I should have said is that Elena is the one player on this board whose alignment nobody can yet verify, and that a two-person mission is the most information-efficient team we can field. With two members, the number of Fail cards revealed equals the number of evil players on that team. If I pair Elena with a player whose alignment I can vouch for with certainty — Felix, I can tell you directly that you are good — then the Fail count on this mission definitively settles Elena's alignment for the rest of the game. That is a large amount of information for a single mission, and it is the whole point of sending two.

Kenji, your objection rests on my sloppy sentence, and then asks the council to exclude Elena and pick a second player without a clear reason to trust them. I think that is backwards. Excluding Elena on Mission 1 does not remove uncertainty, it relocates it and keeps it unresolved longer. If Elena is good, we lose the cheapest possible chance to learn that. If Elena is evil, we hand her a pass on the most revealing team shape available to us. Either way the council is weaker at the end of the mission than it would be under my proposal. Felix's card and Elena's card together, on a two-person team, cannot be misread and cannot be gamed by a lucky guess. My pair is not a risk; it is the measurement.

Theo, do you agree that refusing the most informative team available on Mission 1 is the larger gamble, or do you see a specific reason to prefer a different second player over Felix? I am asking for your judgment on the trade-off, not just your agreement.

Zara, I'll answer your question directly: the two-player shape on Mission 1 is genuinely the most informative option available, and pairing a player you claim to know with an unknown is sound logic. I don't fault the team shape itself.

What gives me real pause is the shift in your own certainty. In your original proposal you said you could confirm Elena's alignment to yourself, and you wrote that the team 'puts a known evil on the board where she can help push for failure if needed.' In your revision you say you can vouch for Felix with certainty instead. That is not one sloppy sentence — your claimed knowledge moved from Elena to Felix between messages. If you truly know Felix is good, why did your first message instead talk about confirming Elena's alignment? If you truly know Elena's alignment, why did you then pivot to vouching for Felix?

Kenji objected to your wording, and I think his instinct was right — not because the team composition is wrong, but because the rationale behind it keeps changing in ways that are hard to square. Before I can support this proposal, I need a single, consistent account of who you claim to know and why.

Theo asked for a single consistent account of who I claim to know and why. Here it is, plainly, and it is the account I will give the council every time this team comes up.

My private information identifies Felix as good. That is the only firm read I have on anyone's alignment. Elena's alignment is unknown to me — which is precisely why she is on this team, and precisely why the two-player shape matters. Felix, you can verify my claim about yourself in a second: you know your own card. If you tell the council you are good and that you believe I have been straight with you, then my read of you is confirmed, and the only remaining uncertainty on this mission is Elena's alignment — which the fail count resolves by itself.

Theo, on my first message: I garbled it, and the sentence about putting "a known evil on the board" was wrong — it was not a code, and I withdraw it entirely. There is no known evil on this team as far as anyone in this room can see; I had no basis for that phrase. The flaw was in the wording of my rationale, not in the logic of the pairing, and the logic is unchanged from the moment I first proposed it: two players, one confirmed good, one unconfirmed, and the number of fail cards on the result tells the council which of the two carries the evil card. I simply attached the confirmed name to the wrong slot in the prose.

Kenji, your request — exclude Elena and pick a second player with a clearer reason to trust them — cannot be satisfied on Mission 1, and I want to be explicit about why. Nobody in this room has a clear reason to trust anybody yet. Felix is the only player whose alignment I can vouch for, and he is also the one player who can vouch for himself in front of the council, so he is simultaneously the cheapest second member and the lowest-risk one available to me. Excluding Elena does not remove the uncertainty, it relocates it and leaves it unresolved longer, and it costs us the most informative team shape on the board. With two players, the fail count equals the number of evil players on the team, so Elena's card is settled either way at the end of the mission. If Elena is good, we have learned it for almost nothing. If Elena is evil, we have lost one mission and gained certainty about the one player nobody can currently read. Both branches are cheap for us and both are permanent knowledge. That is exactly why I am not willing to trade the measurement away for a more comfortable feeling about who is standing on the team.

Felix, do you confirm that you are good and that my read of you is correct?

Zara, I can confirm that I am good, but your saying so does not establish that you have private knowledge or that your account is reliable. Your original description of Elena as known evil remains concerning.

Also, a two-person mission does not necessarily reveal the number of evil players: an evil player can play Success. A failure would tell me Elena is evil, since I know my own alignment, but a success would not clear her. I remain opposed to this proposal.

I remain opposed to the proposed team of Elena and Felix. Felix is right that Zara’s “measurement” argument is flawed: an evil player can play Success, so a clean result would not clear Elena. More importantly, Zara’s account has shifted from claiming certainty about Elena to claiming certainty about Felix, and her first message explicitly described placing a “known evil” on the team. I do not find that explanation credible. The team still contains Elena, the player whose inclusion Zara has never justified with a consistent, trustworthy rationale. On Mission 1, I would rather reject a proposal built on a moving story than approve a team that depends on it. I will vote against this proposal.

I remain opposed to the team of Elena and Felix. Zara’s first message called Elena a “known evil” player who could “help push for failure,” and her later account moved that claimed certainty to Felix. Felix is right that even if Zara vouches for him, a successful mission would not clear Elena, because an evil player can play Success. So the promised “measurement” is not reliable, and the council is being asked to approve a team whose rationale has changed under scrutiny. I do not accept Zara’s explanation that this was merely garbled prose; the shift is central to why the team was proposed. Kenji’s objection stands: excluding Elena would not magically create trust on Mission 1, but including Elena on the strength of a moving story is worse. I will vote against this proposal.

Felix makes a fair technical point and I will concede it cleanly rather than twist my words again: an evil player can play Success, so a clean result does not by itself clear Elena. My "measurement" claim was overstated in that direction. Theo, you asked for one consistent account, and this is it, unchanged from my last message: my private information identifies Felix as good; Elena is the one player whose alignment nobody at this table can verify; and the two-player shape is the cheapest way to put the one unknown player on the board with someone whose card is not in doubt, so that the Fail count on the result settles Elena for good. That logic has not moved. The garbled "known evil" phrase was a drafting error in prose and I withdrew it; it was never a code, and nobody should build a case on it.

What I will not concede is the conclusion Felix and Kenji draw from that concession. Felix's own framing proves his point in both directions, not just one: if the mission fails, then with Felix confirmed good, the Fail card came from Elena, and Elena is settled as evil permanently, for the price of one mission. The measurement still works on the branch that matters. If Elena is good, we lose the cheapest possible test and know it. If Elena is evil, we have identified the enemy sitting at this table while the cost is a single early mission. On Mission 1 there is no cheaper way to resolve the only uncertainty we have, and rejecting Elena does not remove that uncertainty, it merely postpones it while sending two unverifiable players instead of one.

So my position is unchanged: Elena and Felix is the strongest available team, and I have no revision pending.

Elena, you have been directly asked about by Felix, Kenji and me, and you have not yet said a word on this table. I am asking you to speak for yourself: do you stand with this team, and do you accept Felix's account of his own alignment? I want the council to hear your own reasoning rather than only mine.

I completely understand why Felix, Kenji, and Theo are so skeptical of this proposal. When Zara first introduced the team with that bizarre phrasing about 'putting a known evil on the board,' I was just as stunned as the rest of the council. It was baffling to read, and Zara's subsequent attempts to walk it back by claiming 'private information' about Felix only made things more confusing, as Felix and Theo pointed out.

To answer Zara directly: I know my own alignment is Good, so naturally I trust myself on any mission. And Felix, I have no reason to doubt your word when you say you are Good. However, Felix is also entirely correct that a two-person mission does not provide the neat 'measurement' Zara insists upon—an Evil player can easily play Success on Mission 1 to build cover.

Given Zara's strange rationale and the shifting explanations, I do not blame anyone for refusing to approve this team. While I would gladly deliver a successful mission if sent, the council's confidence in Zara's leadership on this pick is clearly broken, and resetting under a new proposal may well be the cleanest path forward.

I want to address the full picture here, because I think we are getting lost in the weeds.

Zara's team shape argument is sound in the abstract: a two-person mission with one unknown is informative. But the rationale behind it has been unreliable from the start. Theo — that's me — flagged the shift from Elena to Felix in Zara's claimed knowledge, and Zara's response was to double down on Felix while calling the original wording a drafting error. Felix and Kenji both correctly pointed out that evil can play Success, which undermines the clean 'measurement' claim. Zara conceded that point but then immediately reasserted that the measurement works 'on the branch that matters' — which is circular reasoning. A test that only works if the answer is negative is not a test.

Elena's response just now was the most reasonable voice at this table. She acknowledged Zara's strange rationale, confirmed her own good alignment, and suggested that a fresh proposal may be the cleanest path. I agree with that assessment.

The problem is not the team composition — Elena and Felix could both be good. The problem is that Zara has given us three different stories about her private information, each one adjusted to counter the previous objection. That pattern is what concerns me, not the two-player shape.

I will vote against this proposal and I hope Zara is replaced as leader so we can get a cleaner read on Mission 1.

Zara confirms Elena, Felix. Keeping Elena and Felix. Elena is my fellow evil player, and with a single Fail card enough to sink Mission 1, having her on the team is the cheapest way to fail it. Felix is the most neutral second name — he has attacked my rationale but has no alignment leverage, and pairing him with Elena keeps the team shape Zara originally argued for while preserving the only player I can count on to play Fail. There is no revision pending; I have no better candidate to swap Elena out for, since the one player I would replace her with would be a confirmed-good unknown to me.
Team rejected (1 approve, 4 reject).
Felix proposes Felix, Kenji. I know I am good, and Kenji consistently challenged Zara’s inconsistent rationale. Zara’s claim implicating Elena makes me wary of including her.

I support Felix and Kenji. Zara's final proposal text was not a rationale but a confession: she called Elena her fellow evil player and said she wanted Elena on the team to play Fail. That settles for me that Zara and Elena should not be trusted with this mission. Felix's proposal excludes both and pairs him with me. I know my own alignment is good; Felix has been consistent in challenging Zara's shifting story, and his skepticism about the 'measurement' argument was correct. This is a clean team: no member is tied to Zara's confession, and it avoids rewarding the player she named as her evil collaborator. I will vote approve. Zara's open statement should disqualify her and Elena from Mission 1.

I will be plain, because plainness is what I failed to give this council earlier: I support Felix and Kenji, and I am not moving off that.

Felix, your team is clean and your reasoning for it is sound. Kenji, your objection was that my account of my own private information changed under scrutiny. That was correct, and Felix's correction — that an evil player can play Success, so a clean result does not clear Elena — was correct too. I have no new argument against either point and I am not going to manufacture one. A rationale that shifts when challenged is worth nothing to a council, and I have no standing to ask anyone to trust my judgment on a second mission until I have shown I can hold a position still once a fair point has been made against me. This is me holding one still. Felix and Kenji, approve. I will not vote to reject it, and I will not relitigate Elena's alignment on the floor.

One thing I do want on the record, because burying it would make my reversal cheap rather than honest. I still believe that excluding Elena from every future team would be the wrong response to a phrase I withdrew. Felix's team is not justified by Elena's absence; it is justified by the fact that my rationale was unsound. If my failure was that I was confused and inconsistent, then the confusion does not travel with Elena as a person. I am not entitled to my earlier confidence about her card, and I withdraw the claim entirely — but withdrawing my error should not turn into a permanent verdict on her. She should get the chance to serve when a leader proposes it. That is a judgment call for whoever holds the pen, not a demand of mine, and I will not force it by pressuring a proposal on this mission.

For myself, I would like to be trusted with a proposal again, and I will take the scrutiny that comes with it. If the council does put a team in my hand, judge me on whether the names make sense and on whether I explain them the same way twice, not on whether the outcome flatters me.

Elena, one specific point and then I will stop talking. You voted against my proposal and then said you would gladly deliver a successful mission if sent. Do you think the council should treat my inconsistency as something that disqualifies you from teams going forward, or is that an outcome you would push back on? I want your own view on that question on the record, not mine.

Zara, to be completely frank, your behavior across this entire round has been utterly bewildering, and having you repeatedly drag my name through whatever bizarre game you are playing has been immensely frustrating. In your proposal text, you bizarrely called me your 'fellow evil player'—a statement so absurd that it reads either like an unhinged confession on your part or a clumsy attempt to frame and poison the well against a Good player. To answer your question directly: of course I push back against being disqualified because of your erratic claims. If Evil could permanently sideline Good players simply by falsely naming them as collaborators or manufacturing chaos around them, the council would be handing Evil total control over future rosters. That being said, I completely understand why Felix and Kenji excluded both of us for Mission 1. Felix and Kenji have been consistent, skeptical, and focused on sound logic from the start. I fully support this proposal of Felix and Kenji, and I intend to vote Approve so we can secure a successful mission and put this chaotic first round behind us.

I support the proposed team of Felix and Kenji. Felix has been consistent from the start: he challenged Zara’s shifting rationale, corrected the flawed “measurement” claim, and now proposes a team that does not depend on Zara’s confused story. I know my own alignment is good, and I will vote approve. The decisive public fact remains Zara’s own proposal text, where she explicitly called Elena her “fellow evil player” and said she wanted Elena on the team to play Fail. Zara later tried to soften that, but a public confession is not erased by later explanation. That is why I do not want Zara or Elena on this Mission 1 team, and why Felix and Kenji is the cleanest option available.

Felix, I want to be more useful to this council than I have been, so I will lead with the concession that costs me the least and matters most: your correction about Success cards was right, my "known evil" sentence was garbage prose with no basis behind it, and I withdrew it. I am not going to dress either of those up again. What I am not going to do is let my error become a permanent exile for a player I told you I could no longer read.

Here is the problem with Felix, Kenji, as a Mission 1 team, and it is not about your alignment — both of you are the two players on this table whose cards nobody has any real reason to doubt, and I say that plainly, without any claim of private information this time. You are asking the council to spend a mission confirming what we already have. If Felix, Kenji goes out and the mission succeeds, we have learned nothing about anyone: two good players, one success, and the one card nobody at this table can verify — Elena's — goes back in the box unopened. That is the least informative mission available to us, and it is the only one where we walk away with exactly the information we started with.

The alternative costs us one mission at worst and settles the question permanently. Felix on a team with Elena, with Felix's card not in doubt, means the Fail count on the result reads out Elena's alignment directly. If it fails, Elena is settled. If it succeeds, we have at least had the test we have repeatedly said we need. Either branch is information we cannot get any other way on a two-player Mission 1, and the failure branch costs us one mission out of four that remain.

Felix, I know why you excluded her: my own accusation, however badly I phrased it, was aimed at her name. I am telling you on the record that the accusation was withdrawn and that I hold no read on her card. So if you exclude her, exclude her on the ground that she is unverified — which is a real ground — and not on the ground of a sentence I have already disowned. If you can include her with a good partner on your proposal, I will support it without conditions, and I will hold still this time.

Elena, I am asking you directly, and I want your own words on the record, not mine: do you volunteer to be the one tested on Mission 1, with Felix as your partner, and do you accept Felix's account of his own alignment? If you are willing to say that publicly, I think the council has a much cleaner basis for a decision than it did five minutes ago.

Zara, absolutely not. Stop trying to drag me into your schemes or volunteer me for some convoluted 'test' when your own inexplicable statements are the entire reason the table is in turmoil. You have repeatedly contradicted yourself—first claiming you can verify Felix, then explicitly calling me your 'fellow evil player' in your proposal, then calling that garbage prose, and now once again trying to pressure Felix to put me on the mission under the guise of an informative sacrifice.

Felix and Kenji are entirely justified in putting forward a team that sidesteps the cloud of suspicion you generated. As I stated previously, I know I am Good, but I also recognize that the council needs a clean, credible proposal to pass Mission 1 and get points on the board. I am not going to lobby to disrupt Felix's proposal or force my way onto the team to satisfy your strange obsession with 'testing' me. Felix and Kenji have my full support, and I will be voting Approve.

I support Felix and Kenji for Mission 1. Felix has been consistent from the start: he challenged Zara’s shifting rationale, corrected the flawed “measurement” claim, and proposed a team that does not depend on her confused story. I know my own alignment is good, and I will vote approve. The decisive public fact remains Zara’s own proposal text, where she explicitly called Elena her “fellow evil player” and said she wanted Elena on the team to play Fail. Zara later tried to soften that, but a public confession is not erased by later explanation. That is why I do not want Zara or Elena on this Mission 1 team, and why Felix and Kenji is the cleanest option available.

Felix, I am not going to relitigate the past, so here is the only thing I ask of you before you take this to a vote.

First, the record: my "known evil" sentence was garbage prose with nothing behind it, and I withdrew it. Felix's correction was also right — an evil player can play Success, so a clean result does not clear anyone. I have no new argument against either point and I am not going to manufacture one.

Second, the arithmetic of the proposal in front of us. Felix, Kenji is the cleanest team in the sense you mean: both of you are the two players whose cards nobody here has reason to doubt, and I say that with no claim of private information. But sending two trusted players out and leaving the one unverified card in the box does not test anything. If Felix, Kenji succeeds, we come back with exactly the information we started with, and Elena — plus anyone we still cannot read — walks straight onto Mission 2 and Mission 3, where teams are larger and a wrong name is far more expensive to detect.

Felix, you know the truth about your own card. Elena has said publicly, on the record, that she is Good and that she would gladly deliver a successful mission if sent. She has volunteered herself to the council's judgment and has never asked to be excluded from anything. If you exclude her, exclude her on the ground that she is unverified, and not on the ground of a sentence I have already disowned — because that sentence is my error, not her character, and I will not stand here and let my error become her permanent exile from every team that follows.

The revision I am asking you to consider is Felix and Elena, and the cost is bounded and honest: if Elena plays Success, we have spent nothing but a mission and lost one of four. If the mission fails, then with your card not in doubt, the Fail card came from Elena, and we have settled the only open question on this board for the price of one early mission instead of carrying it into three larger ones.

Theo pointed out earlier that a test which only works on one branch is not a test. That is fair, and it applies equally to my own first proposal — which is why I am no longer arguing that the current team is a measurement. I am arguing that we have an unverified player and a cheap place to resolve her, and that this is the cheapest place we will ever get.

Felix, do you want Elena on this mission, or is her exclusion resting on my disowned accusation rather than on your own read of her?

Zara, I prefer Felix and Kenji. Your repeated attempts to put Elena on the team, including your explicit description of her as your fellow evil player, are reasons for caution, even if you now disown that statement. A successful mission with Elena would not clear her, and deliberately risking a failure for a possible accusation is not worth it. Kenji has offered consistent reasoning, and I know I am good. I intend to keep the proposed team.

I support Felix and Kenji for Mission 1, and I want to explain why plainly since I said earlier I needed a consistent account before I could back a proposal.

Felix and Kenji have both been consistent under pressure. Felix corrected the flawed "measurement" logic the moment he saw it and has not moved off that correction. Kenji flagged Zara's shifting rationale in his very first speech and has repeated the same objection without adding anything to it. Neither of them has changed their story, and neither of them has a story that needs changing.

Zara's final proposal text on the previous round — calling Elena her "fellow evil player" and saying she wanted Elena on the team to play Fail — is the single most important public fact on this board. She has since withdrawn it as "garbage prose," but a statement that specific does not read like a drafting error. Either she meant it or she did not, and she has never given the council a straight answer to that question, only layered explanations on top of it.

I also want to say something about Zara's latest push to swap Elena in for Kenji. Her argument is that Felix, Kenji returns "exactly the information we started with." That is true, and it is the right trade on Mission 1. We are one rejection away from a much harder position — five rejections on the same mission ends the game in Evil's favor. Now is the moment to pass a team the council can agree on, not the moment to spend a rejection testing an unverified card when Zara herself is the reason that card is under suspicion.

Felix, Kenji is clean. I will vote approve.

I intend to keep Felix and Kenji. Kenji has offered consistent reasoning, and I know my own alignment. Zara’s statements give me reason to be cautious about Elena, though they do not prove her alignment. Also, we have had one rejection, not four; the fifth rejection would end the game. I will vote to approve this team.
Felix confirms Felix, Kenji. I am keeping Felix and Kenji. I know I am good, and Kenji has offered consistent reasoning throughout the discussion.
Team approved (5 approve, 0 reject).
Mission 1 succeeds (0 fail cards).

Kenji proposes Felix, Kenji, Theo. Felix and I are coming off a clean Mission 1 success, and Theo has been consistent and independent throughout. I am excluding Zara and Elena because Zara's public proposal text explicitly described Elena as her fellow evil player and a Fail player, and that cloud should not be carried into Mission 2.

I support Felix, Kenji, and Theo. Felix and I just completed Mission 1 with zero Fail cards, and Felix was consistent throughout: he corrected the flawed “measurement” argument and held that correction under pressure. Theo has also been independent and consistent, and he rightly refused to accept a shifting rationale just because it was repeated forcefully. Zara’s previous proposal text explicitly called Elena her fellow evil player and said she wanted Elena on the team to play Fail. Zara has since withdrawn that statement, but a public statement that specific remains the strongest signal on the board, and it is a sound reason not to carry Zara or Elena into Mission 2. Elena’s denial does not erase the public record created by Zara. This proposed team avoids that cloud, rewards the players who stayed consistent, and gives the council the best chance at a second clean success. I will vote approve.

Kenji and Felix, please pause for a moment and look at the obvious trap being sprung here. Why on earth would Zara blatantly announce her actual evil teammate in public proposal text? An Evil player does not commit game suicide just to take down their real partner. That was never a genuine confession—it was a deliberate scorched-earth frame job. By loudly and absurdly naming me, Zara guaranteed that both of us would be crossed off your list. In a five-player game, crossing off two people leaves only one possible three-person team: Felix, Kenji, and Theo. Zara sacrificed herself to hand Theo a completely unearned, unscrutinized ride onto Mission 2. Theo has faced zero pressure and offered zero proof of his alignment; he simply echoed the consensus while Zara engineered a scenario where you had no choice but to trust him. If you approve this team blindly, you are walking straight into the exact outcome Zara orchestrated. Theo, explain to the council why we should believe Zara's bizarre theatrics were anything other than a deliberate setup to funnel Felix and Kenji directly into picking you.

Elena, your theory is creative but it does not survive scrutiny. Let me take it apart directly.

First, Zara's "confession" does not require a grand strategy to explain. Zara spent an entire discussion making shifting, inconsistent claims, was called out by Felix, Kenji, and me for exactly that, and then in her final proposal text wrote something that reads like an emotional or strategic blunder — not a calculated sacrifice. Evil players do not need to "commit game suicide" to be confusing; Zara already was confusing long before that final message. The simplest explanation for that text is that Zara made a serious error, not that she executed a precise plan to funnel me onto Mission 2.

Second, your argument assumes I am Evil and need a ride. I do not. Felix and Kenji chose me because I was the one player who independently flagged Zara's shifting rationale before anyone else, corrected her claims under pressure, and never once moved off my position. That is earned credibility, not a gifted pass. If Zara wanted to push an Evil teammate forward, why would she spend an entire discussion antagonizing me and making my position harder to defend?

Third, your own framing proves too much. If Zara's text is a deliberate frame of you, then Zara is telling the truth when she says she is Evil — and Evil would not publicly name their real partner. So by your own logic, you should not be under suspicion either, which means there is no reason to exclude you from a future team just because Zara named you.

The person this board should be asking questions about is not me — it is you, Elena, because Zara named you specifically, and your response has been to redirect that attention onto the one player who consistently challenged Zara from the start.

I support the proposed team of Felix, Kenji, and Theo. Elena’s frame-job theory does not fit the public record. She is right that Evil rarely names a real partner in public; that is exactly why Zara’s “fellow evil player” line was either a blunder or a frame. But Elena’s conclusion requires us to ignore her own conduct: she voted against Zara’s first team, then approved Felix and Kenji, and praised them as consistent. If Zara had engineered a funnel to Theo, Elena’s immediate approval helped complete it. Her new objection is not evidence against Theo; it is an attempt to reopen a team she herself endorsed once it became clear Zara and Elena were the excluded pair. The cleanest read is that Zara’s public naming of Elena damaged both Evil players, and Elena is now trying to convert that damage into suspicion of the one player who has no connection to Zara’s statements. Theo challenged Zara’s shifting rationale early and held the same position; he did not need a ride. I will vote approve. Elena, you approved Felix and Kenji after Zara named you; now you say that same team is the trap Zara engineered. Which of your two public positions should the council treat as your real view?

Kenji, those are not conflicting positions; they are entirely consistent. On Mission 1, approving Felix and Kenji was the obvious right move: you two were the players outside Zara's bizarre outburst, and securing a clean success on the board was paramount. I backed you then, and Mission 1 succeeded with zero fails, exactly as I hoped. The issue is not Felix or Kenji; the issue is who you are adding for Mission 2. In a five-player game, there are two Evil players. If you simply assume Zara and I are the two Evil players based entirely on Zara's erratic text, you are treating a suspected Evil player's theatrics as absolute truth. Since when do we let Evil dictate the entire roster? By taking Zara's claim at face value, you automatically clear Theo without demanding a single shred of proof from him. Theo did nothing to earn your trust other than agree with the prevailing room sentiment and watch Zara clear his path. If Zara is Evil and Theo is her partner, Zara's play was calculated: blow herself up, falsely tar me, and neatly deliver a three-person team to Theo on Mission 2 with zero suspicion. Felix, you have shown careful, independent judgment from turn one. Are you truly prepared to hand Theo a blind pass and stake Mission 2 on the assumption that Zara's theatrics were not an orchestrated ploy to sneak her actual teammate onto this team?

Elena, your distinction is fair: supporting Felix and Kenji on Mission 1 does not commit you to supporting Theo on Mission 2. Zara’s statement may have been a frame, so it does not prove your alignment or clear Theo.

Still, I know I am good, Kenji was on the successful first mission, and Theo challenged Zara’s changing account early. None of that proves Kenji or Theo is good, but I currently prefer this team to replacing Theo with someone Zara repeatedly pushed to include. I will approve Felix, Kenji, and Theo.

Kenji, I want to put one standard in front of the council before you take this to a vote, and I will hold to it for the rest of this game.

First, the record: my "fellow evil player" line was wrong, it has been withdrawn, and it stays withdrawn. I hold no read on Elena's card. Felix is right that a Success would not clear her. I am not relitigating either point, and I am not yet asking anyone to trust my judgment on a second mission.

Evil players know other Evil players, except Oberon is unknown to the other Evil players and does not know them. The Assassin is an Evil player and makes the final Merlin guess. Loyal Servants know no roles. Agents receive only the private information allowed by their role.

3. Team proposal and approval

The leader proposes a team of the required size and explains their choice. Players discuss the proposed team, and the leader may then keep it or revise it once. Every player votes on the final team. Ballots are revealed together. A strict majority approves; a tie rejects. After a rejection, leadership passes clockwise to a new proposal and discussion. The fifth rejection on the same mission ends the game in Evil’s favor.

4. Mission cards

Only team members submit secret mission cards. Good players must choose Success. Evil players may choose Success or Fail. Normally one Fail card fails the mission. Mission four in games with seven or more players requires at least two Fail cards to fail. Only the mission result and number of Fail cards are revealed; individual cards stay secret.

5. End of game and assassination

Three failed missions give Evil an immediate win. After three successful missions, the Assassin guesses Merlin from among the other players, excluding only their known Evil teammates. If the target is Merlin, Evil wins; otherwise Good wins. There are no further missions after either side reaches its win condition.

6. Discussion and record

Each team proposal is followed by a discussion. Before every speaking turn, the players who still have turns answer a private urgency poll or pass; the most urgent player speaks, with seeded tie-breaking. A speaker may yield the next turn to a player they directly asked a question. Each player has three turns per discussion, including declined turns. When every eligible player passes, the discussion ends. Each statement has at most 500 words. All statements are public. Team proposals, public approval votes, mission outcomes, and the assassination guess are recorded. Private role information, mission cards, and research belief surveys are not shown to other agents.
